pradeep: Quick heads-up — ran a cross-quant bake on new-70B (chat-prefixed workload) comparing AWQ, GPTQ, INT8, FP8 with our continuous-batching + prefix prefetch stack. Saw an odd KV hit entropy effect when AWQ+int8 ran with prefetch enabled; cache-hit rate dropped ~8-12% for long prefixes and latency jitter rose.
ella: Can you drop the minimal numbers? what was the eval metric delta (MRR / exact-match / ppl)?
pradeep: MRR on our 10k eval set: baseline fp16=0.745, AWQ_int8=0.737 (−1.07%), GPTQ ~0.742 (−0.40%), FP8 ~0.743 (−0.27). Not catastrophic but consistent on prefix-heavy conversations. lat_p50 p90 increased by ~10ms/35ms for AWQ_int8 under cont-batching with prefetch on.
sasha: Interesting. Is the kv cache serving stale keys or misses due to quant noise? any evidence in kv hit time-series? maybe collisions from compacted keys?
pradeep: Time-series shows abrupt drop in prefix-kv_hit where prefetch window overlaps batch assembly. Looks correlated with cont-batcher grouping incoming requests earlier (short timeout) -> prefetch launched on partial context -> kv entries inserted that get overwritten by later chunks due to AWQ's small-value quant rounding producing different key fingerprints.
sam_dev: Wait, key "fingerprints" changed? Shouldn't kv keys be exact token-position lexical keys? is this numeric mismatch at FP compare level or hash upstream?
pradeep: The runtime hashes the key bytes (post-quantized KV). AWQ int8 quant produces slightly different bytes vs fp16/GPTQ, so the hash differs if prefetch happens before full prefix normalization. So two racey inserts for same logical prefix can happen.
ci-bot: [deploy] perf/prod-prefetch-toggle -> rolled to canary in infra-dev
tess: Any repro in offline deterministic run? can we craft a microtest that simulates short inter-arrival times + cont-batching?
pradeep: Yes, added unit reproducer in /tmp/kv_entropy_repro.py, steps:
```
# simplified repro
python kv_entropy_repro.py --model new-70b-awq --quant awq-int8 --prefetch true --cont_batch_timeout 6ms --requests 5000
```
Results show kv_hit drop 9% vs same run with prefetch=false. Full logs: `kv_hits: 91%, 82%` when prefetch on.
ella: Good. Any mitigation without reverting quant profile? can we change prefetch gating or kvcache keying?
sasha: Options: 1) gate prefetch when quantized model active + cont-batch timeout < X, 2) normalize prefetch to wait for full prefix commit, 3) change key to include sequence-id + stable serialization before quantization.
sam_dev: (2) sounds impactful to latency. (1) could be a pragmatic quick fix: turn prefetch off for AWQ_int8 on routes that are prefix-heavy.
pradeep: Agreed. I prototyped (1): small perf regression in cold token latency but stable kvcache rate. Implemented feature flag `prefetch.quant-aware=false` default true; we flip for AWQ_int8 route in canary.
tess: Any rollout plan if canary passes? metrics to watch?
pradeep: Watch kv_hit_pct, MRR_eval, p90 latency, and regression alerts on quality. Canary -> 5% -> 20% -> full. If MRR drops >0.5% revert.
ella: Also add an eval job paired with canary that runs the 10k eval set on rollout to catch silent regressions.
sasha: Long term fix = change keying serialization to use stable-pre-quant bytes. Filed infra ticket INF-3281.
pradeep: Filed ML ticket ML-1292 for quant-aware prefetch gating + repro + experiments. Will also run AWQ quant variants (per-layer mixed-quant) to see if that reduces kv-byte churn.
sam_dev: Nice. Anything we should change in batching heuristics? cont-batcher timeout tweak maybe?
pradeep: Setting cont-batch timeout from 6ms -> 12ms reduced the race window and improved hit-rate but increased p50 by ~6ms. Might be acceptable for backend routes; depends on SLA.
tess: Ok please post the canary link and repro script. thanks.
pradeep: Pushed repro + canary config: https://ci.internal/runs/1934001290 and PR #8793. I'll monitor and post update in this thread. :thumbsup:
ci-bot: [note] PR #8793 opened by pradeep: disable prefetch for awq-int8 on chat-prefixed route (canary)
pradeep: Update (1934001605): canary at 5% shows kv_hit stable and MRR delta reduced to −0.2% (within noise). continuing 20% -> 100% ramp if stable.
